🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Regina Torné, the Mexican actress best known as the formidable Mamá Elena in Como agua para chocolate and as Tía Gloria in El Chavo del 8, has died at 82.

Torné died on November 11, 2026, at her home in Mexico City, according to Mexico's National Actors Association (ANDA), which confirmed her death. Her passing was reported by El Universal, El Financiero and Reforma. No cause of death has been disclosed.

Born in Villahermosa, Tabasco, Torné began her artistic career as a jazz singer before moving into film in the 1960s, becoming one of the familiar faces of Mexican cinema in the 1960s and 1970s. Her defining film role came in 1992, when she played Mamá Elena, the stern matriarch, in Alfonso Arau's Como agua para chocolate, based on the novel by Laura Esquivel — one of the most celebrated Mexican films ever made. She won an Ariel Award, Mexico's top film honor, for best actress.

To television audiences across Latin America, she was Tía Gloria, the aunt of Paty, who joined Roberto Gómez Bolaños' beloved series El Chavo del 8 in 1978. She worked in film, theater and television for more than six decades, including telenovelas such as La Loba and Cielo Rojo.

Sources: El Universal; El Financiero; Reforma; Asociación Nacional de Actores (ANDA).
